# Kāmāvacarakusala (Ds 2.1.1)

**ID:** Ds 2.1.1
**Section:** Dhammasaṅgaṇī (ds)
**Collection:** Abhidhamma
**Title (Pali):** Kāmāvacarakusala
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/abh01m.mul1.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kāmāvacarakusala* ("Wholesome [Consciousness] of the Sense Sphere") is the opening analytical section of the *Cittuppādakaṇḍa* (the book on the arising of consciousness) in the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the first treatise of the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Hazra 1994]. Following the matrix (*mātikā*) of wholesome phenomena (*kusala-dhammā*), the text systematically analyzes sense-sphere wholesome states (*kāmāvacara-kusala-dhammā*) by distinguishing eight fundamental types of consciousness (*citta*) [Gethin 2001; Bodhi 1999]. These eight consciousnesses are categorized through three intersecting dichotomies: affective tone, divided between mental joy (*somanassa*) and equanimity (*upekkhā*); cognitive orientation, being either associated with knowledge (*ñāṇasampayutta*) or dissociated from it (*ñāṇavippayutta*); and volitional activation, whether unprompted (*asaṅkhārika*) or prompted (*sasaṅkhārika*) [Bodhi 1999]. For each consciousness type, the text presents an exhaustive inventory of its constituent mental factors (*cetasika*), such as contact (*phassa*) and volition (*cetanā*) [Devdas 2004]. In her study and translation of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, C. A. F. Rhys Davids notes the distinctive canonical phraseology of the manual (such as *kāmāvacaraṁ kusalaṁ*) in contrast to later commentarial idiom [Rhys Davids 1900].

**Parallels and text reuse**

- Passage-level parallels: Cnd 17 Udayamāṇavapucchāniddesa; Mnd 16 Sāriputtasuttaniddesa; Cnd 23 Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa; Cnd 5 Ajitamāṇavapucchāniddesa; Mnd 8 Pasūrasuttaniddesa; Mnd 2 Guhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa
- Resembling parallels: Mnd 6 Jarāsuttaniddesa; Ds 2.2.3 Rūpavibhatti

**Sources**

- [Bodhi 1999] Bhikkhu Bodhi (ed.), A Comprehensive Manual of Abhidhamma (1999) — Analysis and division of the eight types of sense-sphere wholesome consciousness (kāmāvacara-kusalacittāni) by three principles of dichotomization.
- [Devdas 2004] Nalini Devdas, A Study of Cetanā and the Dynamics of Volition in Theravāda Buddhism (PhD thesis, 2004) — Enumeration of mental factors in unprompted sense-sphere wholesome consciousness.
- [Gethin 2001] R. M. L. Gethin, The Buddhist Path to Awakening: A Study of the Bodhi-Pakkhiya Dhammā (2001 [1992]) — Contextualization of kāmâvacara-kusala within the Dhammasaṅgaṇī's structural grouping of dhammas.
- [Hazra 1994] Kanai Lal Hazra, Pāli Language and Literature (1994) — Sequence of topics in the Dhammasaṅgaṇī leading into kāmāvacarakusalam.
- [Rhys Davids 1900] Caroline A. F. Rhys Davids, A Buddhist Manual of Psychological Ethics (1900) — Textual and grammatical analysis of the Dhammasaṅgaṇī's phrasing of kāmāvacarakusala versus commentarial idiom.
